claims.text: Chemical short-range order suppresses lattice thermal conductivity in concentrated RHEAs below the order-disorder transition temperature.
The proposed conductivity suppression is caused by diffuse antiphase boundaries acting as phonon-scattering centers.
As temperature approaches or exceeds the ODTT, entropy disrupts SRO and restores phonon mean free paths toward random-solid-solution values.
A MoNbTaW random solid solution can be converted to an SRO state by equilibration at 800 K.
Negative Warren-Cowley parameters for selected atomic pairs indicate chemical ordering.
An ODTT of approximately 1120 K is an applicable guide for MoNbTaW or similar RHEAs.
DAPBs form locally as phonons traverse chemically ordered regions.
Breaking local chemical order has an energy cost that can produce a fluctuating potential landscape for phonons.
SRO produces periodic or semiperiodic variations in atomic mass and bonding stiffness on the scale of the phonon mean free path.
Scattering in the random solid solution is isotropic, whereas SRO produces specific phonon-scattering resonances.
SRO-associated DAPBs act as additional phonon-scattering interfaces and raise the scattering rate above that of the random solid solution.
An increased phonon scattering rate reduces lattice thermal conductivity.
The SRO sample should have lower lattice thermal conductivity than the RSS sample between approximately 300 and 800 K.
The thermal-conductivity difference should decrease monotonically with temperature and converge to zero at the ODTT.
SRO is stable below the ODTT and tends toward zero upon disordering at the ODTT.
Phonon scattering by SRO may be weak when the SRO correlation length is much smaller than the dominant phonon wavelength.
In simulated MoNbTaW, SRO creates DAPBs during dislocation glide and changes dislocation mobility through an associated energy cost.
The cited evidence does not directly quantify thermal conductivity or phonon scattering caused by SRO in RHEAs.
Quenching can retain an RSS state, while annealing at 800 K followed by rapid cooling can preserve an SRO state for comparison.
Equal or greater lattice thermal conductivity in the SRO sample when the measured SRO magnitude exceeds 0.1 would falsify the proposed suppression hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The boundary allows negligible conductivity suppression despite nonzero SRO when the correlation length is much smaller than the phonon wavelength, but the falsification rule treats any absence of suppression at |alpha_1| > 0.1 as decisive without controlling for correlation length.
